status: WRITTEN candidates with WRITTEN-checked-in-kernel examples; not parent adoption
findings: An explicit strictly stable full-width septic box has a known unrestricted common numerator but no common numerator in the REAL span of its four parity endpoints. Five positive actual atoms annihilate the entire span exactly; their cofactor signs also yield an explicit 14-dimensional endpoint neighborhood preserving the obstruction and the fixed common numerator.

In that same box, the four parity endpoints and derivatives D^4..D^7 of the midpoint form a full real basis. A different five-atom functional annihilates the endpoints and is strictly negative on all four high derivatives, so every common numerator has at least one negative high-derivative basis coordinate; this persists in an explicit open neighborhood.

For an open dense subset of the feasible nine-parameter five-contact boundary family, an exact nonzero tangent minor and written compactness show that every sufficiently near-boundary radial stable box lacks a common numerator in its own real endpoint span. This does not claim whether unrestricted synthesis exists.

The conditional ratio-gap no-five-frequency theorem has a 14-dimensional open example in which all four corner numerators fail, but a fixed external numerator succeeds. Another simpler example neighborhood actually has fixed numerator (s+1)^7 and hence excludes certificates of every support; that stronger example disposition is stated in an addendum.
remaining_gap: No actual box with a strict all-numerator negative certificate and no universal positive theorem are established. The genuine obstructions above apply to named numerator subspaces, cones or certificate supports, not to all numerators/frequencies.
next_action: Use the endpoint-span annihilator and full-basis quotient to investigate whether independent actual atoms can obstruct all quotient directions, or derive a universal constructive separator without that restricted span.
